status: Bending components only; torsion excluded. Exact-tip slope is unbounded; global small-rotation assumptions fail.
aeroStatus: Sectional response solved: nominal normal stress and pure-bending components; torsion and aeroelastic feedback not assessed.

notes: Rigid-wing pressures are treated as prescribed loads for a sectional structural study. Admission here assesses numerical load transfer, not strength or full motion. This is not a full aeroelastic admission.

Actual zero tip chord is retained. Force density follows chord and residual free-couple density follows chord squared, conserving all source-strip forces and moments. Local recovery remains a sub-strip projection.

Torsion, shear-centre torque, shear deformation and local 3-D concentrations are not resolved. A delta may have finite formal bending translation and an unbounded tip slope; this does not establish small-rotation validity near the apex. Large inboard rotations require a nonlinear model. Exact-apex stress is undefined.
admission.method: Six-component conservative geometric projection; force and bending uncertainty at the root and 25/50/75% span <=5%, pressure/Trefftz lift agreement <=2%, exact transfer checked independently against the structural cuts. No torsional or aeroelastic claim.

bending.reason: The improper pure-bending translation is finite, but the exact tip slope is unbounded. Small-rotation beam kinematics are not valid arbitrarily close to this apex.

verification.method: Six-component outboard wrench integration and polygon normal-moment recovery
